record.paper_title: On some open problems of Radu
record.original_question: Let T be a triangular norm, meaning a binary operation on [0,1] that is commutative, monotone in both arguments, has T(a,1)=a, and is associative. Let (X,F,T) be a complete generalized Menger space, where Fxy is the probabilistic distance between x and y. For increasing functions alpha:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) and beta:[0,1]->[0,1] with alpha(t)<=t, iterates of alpha tending to 0, beta(u)>=u, gamma(s)=max(alpha(s),1-beta(1-s)) continuous, and the iterated-control series for gamma finite for every s<1, consider a self-map A:X->X satisfying F_{A x,A y}(alpha(t)) >= beta(F_{x y}(t)) for all x,y in X and t>=0, with F_{x,A x}(u)>0 for some x in X and u>0. Which triangular norms T make this contraction principle guarantee that A has a fixed point on every complete generalized Menger space (X,F,T)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm is a binary operation T:[0,1]×[0,1]→[0,1] that is commutative, associative, monotone non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies T(a,1)=a for every a∈[0,1]. A distribution function is a non-decreasing, left-continuous map F:[0,∞)→[0,1] with F(0)=0 and sup F=1. A generalized Menger space is a triple (X,F,T), where X is a non-empty set, T is a triangular norm, and F assigns to every ordered pair (x,y)∈X×X a distribution function F_{x,y} such that:
 (i) F_{x,y}(t)=1 for all t>0 iff x=y,
 (ii) F_{x,y}=F_{y,x},
 (iii) F_{x,z}(t+s) ≥ T(F_{x,y}(t), F_{y,z}(s)) for all x,y,z∈X and t,s≥0.
Equip X with the (ε,λ)-uniformity; (X,F,T) is called complete if every Cauchy sequence in this uniformity converges.

Let α:[0,∞)→[0,∞) and β:[0,1]→[0,1] be non-decreasing functions such that α(t)≤t for all t≥0 and the iterates α^n(t) tend to 0 for every t>0, β(u)≥u for all u∈[0,1], and the function γ(s):=max(α(s), 1−β(1−s)) is continuous. Assume further that for every s<1 the series ∑_{n≥0} γ^n(s) is finite (where γ^n denotes the n-fold iterate of γ as a control function).

Let A:X→X be a self-map satisfying
 F_{Ax,Ay}(α(t)) ≥ β(F_{x,y}(t)) for all x,y∈X and t≥0,
and assume there exists x_0∈X and u_0>0 with F_{x_0,Ax_0}(u_0)>0.

Problem. Characterize the class of triangular norms T such that, for every complete generalized Menger space (X,F,T) and every map A and every pair (α,β) satisfying the hypotheses above, the map A necessarily has a fixed point in X.
artifact.category_tag: probabilistic metric spaces and fixed points
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization is known: V. Radu showed that the continuous t-norms guaranteeing the fixed-point property in this probabilistic contraction setting are precisely those of Hadžić type (H-type), and answers to the listed open problems of Radu, including the one about admissible t-norms for the generalized contraction principle, are provided in subsequent work by Hadžić, Pap, and Radu.

status_evidence.title: A new contraction principle in Menger spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Radu obtained an important result: any continuous t-norm with the fixed point property is of H-type.
status_evidence.claim: The class of admissible continuous t-norms coincides with the H-type t-norms.

status_evidence.title: Fixed Point Results in Generalized Menger Probabilistic Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of generalized contraction mapping principle in probabilistic metric spaces extending Hadžić–Pap–Radu framework.
status_evidence.claim: The contraction principle of Radu in generalized Menger spaces has been resolved via H-type triangular norms.
